title: Off-road vehicles on public lands, implementation of Executive Order 11644 : environmental impact statement.

entities.entity: Department of Commerce, Deputy Assistant Secretary for Environmental Affairs

entities.stance_basis: Suggested clarifications but did not oppose or support the proposed action

entities.entity: Department of Defense, Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense (Environmental Quality)

entities.entity: Department of Health, Education, and Welfare, Assistant Secretary for Health and Scientific Affairs
entities.quote: Department of Health, Education, and Welfare, Assistant Secretary for Health and Scientific Affairs - felt that human impacts portion of environmental statement gave inadequate attention to potential public health hazards associated with use of ORV;

entities.entity: Department of Transportation, Assistant Secretary for Environment and Urban Systems

entities.entity: Environmental Protection Agency, Office of Federal Activities
entities.quote: Environmental Protection Agency, Office of Federal Activities and indicated particular interest in adverse noise impacts of ORV and the measures to be taken to protect the public from noise levels.

entities.entity: Tennessee Valley Authority, Director of Environmental Research and Development

entities.quote: Federal Communications Commission, Chairman - indicated general agreement with the objectives of the environmental statement. entities.quote: Bureau of Reclamation, Acting Commissioner - indicated general concurrence relative to the adequacy of the subject environmental statement;

entities.entity: Bureau of Sport Fisheries and Wildlife, Acting Deputy Director
entities.quote: Bureau of Sport Fisheries and Wildlife, Acting Deputy Director - felt that environmental statement represented a comprehensive statement setting forth criteria for protection of natural resources on Federal lands. Suggested that statement include definitions of ORV, public lands, etc., and define status of ORV use on public lands which are open to mineral entry and established mining claims. Felt that much of the description of economic impacts in the statement is inappropriate and unnecessary. Pointed out that the "open or closed" policies of each of the bureaus should be consistent. Stated belief that completed studies on noise pollution contain enough information for definite acceptable noise levels to be spelled out, in decibels at measured distances, for different types ORV and outdoor public use areas;
entities.stance_basis: Found statement comprehensive but conditioned support on multiple specific improvements

entities.entity: National Park Service, Assistant Director, Cooperative Services

Suggested that evidence be submitted to support claim that ORV can strengthen family ties. Expressed concern about lack of attention in environmental statement to protection of historic, archeological, and paleontological resources.
entities.stance_basis: Supported with conditions including clarifications and compliance assurances for historic preservation laws

entities.quote: We concur with the general approach outlined by the Department for regulating ORV use, and urge that the specific regulations developed by Interior's land managing agencies to designate lands for ORV use contain stringent provisions for: (1) analyzing the environmental impact of the specific types of ORV use contemplated on an area-by-area basis prior to opening any lands; (2) controlling the type and intensity of ORV use in lands opened; (3) monitoring the effects of such use; and, (4) if significant damage to environmental values is occurring, taking prompt corrective measures, including restrictions or prohibition of further ORV use.
entities.stance_basis: Signs EPA letter concurring with general approach but urging stringent provisions

entities.quote: I feel that the Draft Environmental Statement represents a sound approach to the problem of off-road vehicle use of public lands, however the dev to the problem will be the efficacy with which the usage guidelines for these areas are enforced.
entities.stance_basis: Supports draft statement as sound approach but conditions effectiveness on enforcement

entities.quote: On the whole, the proposal is sound and in the interest of all users of public lands. It is evident that, given our society and our standards, some long term damage to the environment cannot be avoided. But we should try to minimize the damage.
entities.stance_basis: Finds proposal generally sound but raises specific objections and doubts about funding/manpower
